items.title: Albert Artigues Sr. Interview, 1961-12-15
items.q: That's why I'm telling you Frank Pattengill opened one of the first twenty-five cent clubs that there was.

ctx.x: Well, what did they have at Bucktown the way the music did they?

Well they didn't have any, any uh, uh, spectacular music. Those days Dick, the cabarets weren't like they ought to do. Man you go to a cabaret at Bucktown it costs you thirty, forty dollars to get out of it. And uh, they didn't go in much for dance bands like they do now. There was more drinking boats than anything else. You didn't go in there and drink. That's why I'm telling you Frank Pattengill opened one of the first twenty-five cent clubs that there was. That was around the twenties. When he opened the…

No, that's all before my time. See I didn't come here until nineteen forty-five. I was in the Navy. Yes. Then I moved here to 49. So it's normal for my time. Yeah. Did they have many solo piano players around town? They had a few.
